title: Microbatch oscillation dampener and KV-hotspot-aware backpressure
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Under sustained high QPS we observe microbatch threshold oscillations that cause transient latency spikes and uneven KV cache churn. This ticket implements a stability layer: (1) an oscillation dampener for microbatch threshold updates using hysteresis + PID-style smoothing, (2) KV-hotspot-aware admission throttling that prefers shedding requests that will cause heavy KV churn or large GPU allocations, and (3) per-priority fairness to prevent tail latency regression for high-priority tenants. Goal is to reduce 99th percentile generation latency regressions and reduce KV eviction cycles under synthetic high-QPS traffic patterns.
acceptance_criteria: 99th percentile latency for our high-QPS benchmark improves by >= 20% compared to baseline without dampener
KV eviction rate (evictions/min) drops by >= 30% under sustained 5x baseline QPS traffic in the hotspot scenario
No regression in average throughput for P0 requests (<= 5% throughput loss) during rollout
Can safely toggle dampener on/off via runtime flag and observe expected metric deltas
Unit and integration tests for dampener logic + KV-hotspot detection merged
tasks: Reproduce oscillation with synthetic harness and capture KV access patterns (done)
Design dampening algorithm: hysteresis window + exponential smoothing + optional integral term
Implement per-priority headroom estimator that factors in KV working set and GPU memory pressure
Add KV-hotspot detector (hot key frequency, shard skew) and label requests likely to cause heavy KV churn
Admission controller: integrate dampener + KV hotspot labels to compute microbatch thresholds and soft-shed candidates
Bench: run A/B against baseline using conflux synthetic driver (3 runs, varying seq lengths and prompt sizes)
Create dashboard panels (latency p50/p90/p99, KV eviction rate, GPU free memory, batch size distribution)
Run gradual canary rollout with traffic split and kill-switch flag
Document algorithm and rollout playbook in Confluence
